commits.message:
An Effect does its per-frame work once a frame, by its shape (rich-effects-caii)

Effect is (t, drawn) => (colors, cell) => colors, and Field and Visibility
are staged the same way. Effected calls the frame stage once per render, so
the three closure caches that asked "same frame as last call?" (atShares,
shimmer, sparkle) are gone, and veiled converts the theme's ground to OKLCH
once a frame instead of once a cell.

onColors settles shares on the colour Effected writes below truecolor (rich-effects-x7y0) (#397)

* onColors settles shares on the colour Effected writes below truecolor (rich-effects-x7y0)

Below truecolor, `shares` checked contrast against `fromRgba(...).downgrade(depth)`
while `Effected` wrote `ColorSpec.matchOn` for the cell's slot, keeping the
written spec when the depth could not show the move. The two disagreed at 256
and 16 colours, so a word could fall below its resting contrast or AA.

The rule now lives once, as `ColorSpec.matchMove`, and both sides call it.
`Pair` gains `reverse`, so each side is matched in the slot it is written in.

* shares reads a pair through the one writer Effected moves a slot with (rich-effects-x7y0)

Effected.shows composites and matches through movedSpecs, the function
respec writes with, so a translucent touch no longer throws in matchOn
and the share check sees the glyph laid on its moved ground. Below
truecolor every written colour is exact, so the 8-bit slack applies only
at truecolor.
Whole-keys settle reads a chunk's rest in full when a sink throws mid-drain (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Whole-keys settle: ESC [ / ESC O is the Alt chord; settling survives a throwing sink (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Review fixes: whole-keys feed no longer runs the split hold logic; header
names InputChunks; docs Input field typed; integration test that a
NodeTerminalHost in the docs worker reads whole-keys. Split-host residue
filed as rich-host-input-gnl7.

A whole-keys host settles each input chunk; no lone ESC is held for a timer (rich-host-input-ab9n)

TerminalHost declares inputChunks: xterm.js (BrowserTerminalHost, and the
docs worker's simulated stdin through NodeTerminalHost) never splits a key
across chunks, so an ESC left at a chunk's end is Escape and what followed
it is re-read. A tty stays "split" and keeps the setTimeout(0) hold.
